title: Iterative pruning: cheap-context PRD jot
content:
Brain dump / rough PRD for 'Iterative Pruning' (working name) — goal: reduce per-request context cost while keeping user-visible continuity for long-running conversations.

Problem statement:
- Customers hit token caps or high cost for long sessions with lots of low-value history (repetitive system messages, chit-chat, long code blocks).
- Need a pragmatic server-side approach that prunes history incrementally with minimal UX churn and measurable cost wins.

Hypothesis:
- If we dynamically identify low-utility turns and replace them with compressed summaries or remove them, token usage drops ~20–50% on average while user-facing coherence remains intact.

User stories:
- As a PM building a chat assistant, I want long conversations to stay cheap so I can keep features enabled for many customers without raising cost.
- As an SRE, I want a predictable pruning policy I can tune per-customer to satisfy latency/cost SLOs.
- As an engineer on private deployments, I want opt-in primitive (config flag + retention windows) so security teams can approve.

Core ideas / approaches to try (ranked):
1) Heuristic-turn removal: drop turns older than N minutes/turns if token-sum above threshold and turns are low-signal (short ephemeral utterances). Cheap to implement.
2) Summarization replace: periodically replace contiguous low-signal turns with 1–2 sentence AI summary stored as single system message. More expensive but better fidelity.
3) Anchor + restore: keep navigation anchors (key facts) and prune other turns; rehydrate via on-demand retrieval if user references prior anchor. Complex.

Signals for low-utility turns (examples):
- Short length (< 8 tokens), repeated quickly, bot confirmations ("ok", "thanks"), ephemeral clarifications.
- Low semantic novelty per embedding distance from recent context.
- Turns mostly code diffs or logs over X lines -> compress or external-store.

API/Config surfaces (first pass):
- pruning.mode = {off | heuristic | summary}
- pruning.window = e.g., 5000 tokens or 200 turns
- pruning.min_signal_threshold = float (0..1) for novelty
- retention.anchors = list of regexes/annotation tags to never prune (e.g., "goal:")
- per-customer override: reserved_capacity customers can set conservative defaults

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Implement heuristic mode server-side and expose flag in SDK/Console.
- End-to-end tests showing >15% token reduction on internal chat benchmarks (average across 10 workloads).
- No regressions in top-5 convo-level coherence evals (micro-evals + human spot checks).
- Telemetry: emit pruning.event with reason, tokens_removed, before_tokens, after_tokens, policy used.

Rollout plan / experiments:
- Field experiment A/B on small subset: baseline vs heuristic-pruning with default window=4000 tokens. Monitor delta in tokens per session, latency, error rate, NPS proxies.
- Parallel run on Dedicated instances to validate resource impact on throughput.

Metrics to track:
- token-saved-per-session (median/95), pct-sessions-pruned, downstream latency impact, coherence-score (micro-eval), cost-savings ($/1000 sessions).

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-pruning loses context -> add conservative defaults, anchors, and automatic rollback heuristics when user asks "remember X" (detect and rehydrate).
- Privacy/regulatory: ensure summary replacement doesn't leak hidden PII; for Private deployments, add opt-in and disable summarization if KMS/HSM constraints.
- Performance: summarization increases token use at pruning time; schedule as background jobs or budget per-session.

Implementation notes / engineering tasks:
- small runtime hook: prune_before_inference(session_state) returns trimmed_state + telemetry. Add unit tests.
- offline eval harness: run on sample corpus (two months chat logs anonymized) and compute savings.
- embed-based novelty detector: prototype with small embedding model (cheap) and threshold tuning.
- add console controls: slider for aggressiveness, audit view showing pruned segments and summaries.

UX sketches (quick):
- Console: per-app toggle + aggressiveness
- In-chat: subtle indicator line "Older messages condensed to save tokens" with expand button to view original block (for allowed customers)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we store raw removed turns for 30d for rehydrate? (tradeoff: storage vs instant restore)
- Which summarization model size? small distil vs medium for higher quality? cost tradeoff.
- Canary signals: what heuristics do we trust first? length + repetition or embeddings + novelty?

Links / references:
- experiment notes: GH PR above, JIRA INF-4212.
- related: session-eviction-playbook (see internal Drive)

Next actions (this week):
- Sync with SRE and product: quick alignment (30m).
- Spin up offline run (anonymized) -> baseline token counts.
- Prototype heuristic prune in runtime local branch (goal: WIP PR by EOW).

Notes-to-self: keep this intentionally rough. Want a low-friction MVP first (heuristic) then iterate with summarization. Think about exposing audit/recovery for enterprise customers to sell as "safe pruning".
